stem: In $\text{BrF}_3$ molecule, the lone pairs occupy equatorial positions to minimize
options: lone pair - bond pair repulsion only
bond pair - bond pair repulsion only
lone pair - lone pair repulsion and lone pair - bond pair repulsion
lone pair - lone pair repulsion only
solution: In $\text{BrF}_3$, both bond pairs as well as lone pairs of electrons are present. Due to the presence of lone pairs of electrons ($lp$) in the valence shell, the bond angle is contracted and the molecule takes the T-shape. This is due to greater repulsion between two lone pairs or between a lone pair and a bond pair than between the two bond pairs.

The rate law expression for the reaction is:
solution:
From slow reaction (rate-determining step):

Rate $= k[\text{A}][\text{B}]$

stem: The reaction, $\text{SO}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \longrightarrow \text{SO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ is exothermic and reversible. A mixture of $\text{SO}_2(g)$, $\text{Cl}_2(g)$ and $\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}_2(l)$ is at equilibrium in a closed container. Now a certain quantity of extra $\text{SO}_2$ is introduced into the container, the volume remaining the same. Which of the following is/are true?
options: The pressure inside the container will not change.
solution: By addition of $\text{SO}_2$ equilibrium will shift to RHS which is exothermic. Hence temperature will increase.

What is the e.m.f for the given cell?
$\text{Cr}|\text{Cr}^{3+}(1.0\text{M})||\text{Co}^{2+}(1.0\text{M})|\text{Co}$
($E^\circ$ for $\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr} = -0.74$ volt and $E^\circ$ for $\text{Co}^{2+}/\text{Co} = -0.28$ volt)
solution:
$E^\circ_{\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}} = -0.74$ V, $E^\circ_{\text{Co}^{2+}/\text{Co}} = -0.28$ V

Cr is anode and Co is cathode.

$E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_C - E^\circ_A = -0.28 - (-0.74) = +0.46$ V

stem: $\text{CH}_3-\overset{\overset{\text{O}}{\|}}{\text{C}}\underset{a}{-}\text{O}\underset{b}{-}\text{CH}_3$; The correct relation between the bond lengths $a$ and $b$ is
solution: Due to resonance, $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{O}^{\delta-})=\overset{\delta+}{\text{O}}-\text{CH}_3$, bond $a$ has partial double bond character. Hence $b > a$.

stem: When electric current is passed through an ionic hydride in molten state:
Number of sigma bonds in $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is
solution:
In the cage structure of $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ there are $12$ bridging P–O bonds and $4$ terminal P=O bonds (each having one $\sigma$ bond).

Number of $\sigma$ bonds $= 12 + 4 = 16$
notes: Printed solution is only the structure; counting text added by transcriber.

stem: The correct order of ligands in the spectrochemical series is

solution: F and O belong to 2nd period whereas Cl and Br belong to 3rd and 4th periods respectively. Hence the sequence of the E.N. is $\text{F} > \text{O} > \text{Cl} > \text{Br}$.
